data.name: Mohanbhai
data.gender_notes: Mohanbhai is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mohan is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'mohana', which means to 'delight' or 'charm'. The prefix 'bhai' means 'brother'. Thus, Mohanbhai can be interpreted as the 'brave brother of the moon'. The name Mohanbhai carries the meaning “Moon, Brave” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Mohanbhai usually hope their child will grow to embody moon, brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Mohanbhai is a divine name associated with Lord Ganesha, who is known as the 'mohana kala' or the 'delighter of the senses'. The name signifies courage, wisdom, and the ability to bring joy and happiness to others.
data.etymology: Mohanbhai belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon, Brave.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mohanbhai total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Mohanbhai Karamchand Gandhi, also known as Mahatma Gandhi, was a prominent Indian nationalist and political leader who led the Indian independence movement against British rule.
historical_references.context: Mohanbhai Gandhi was born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat, India. He was called Mahatma, which means 'great soul', by his followers. Gandhi led nonviolent resistance campaigns against British rule, including the Indian Salt Satyagraha, which led to the end of the British monopoly on salt production. He was assassinated on January 30, 1948.

historical_references.reference: Mohanbhai Dhulia was a Maratha warrior who led a rebellion against the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the late 17th century.
historical_references.context: Mohanbhai Dhulia, also known as Chatrapati Sambhaji, was the son of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the founder of the Maratha Empire in India. After his father's death, Mohanbhai continued the struggle against Mughal rule. He was crowned as Chatrapati, or emperor, in 1674. Mohanbhai faced several military campaigns against the Mughals and other regional powers. He was captured by the Mughals in 1680 and was executed by Emperor Aurangzeb.
